input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: Its ESC_TAU_US comment pointed to `python -m tennisbots esc-lag`, a command that did not exist; this PR adds it.
'An ESC lag picked from the build's own balls' quotes 41-44% spin error for a first-order build told 20-50 ms; on current firmware the 50 ms case reads 12.0% worst (the new section notes the change).
The post date rule (`date -u +%F`) was easy to miss while the local day had turned; I first stamped files 2026-11-17 and had to rename them.

deviations.why: The brief item said 'warn'. A calibration drill now stops before its first ball instead (with --esc-lag-ok to override), because a warning scrolls by while 12 skewed strokes land in the shot log.
deviations.did: hold for calibration drills, warn for the rest
deviations.result: 72-build sweep: every mis-set board held, none after re-flash

deviations.why: node platform/pages/venture-preflight.mjs was not run: the change is firmware/host Python plus README, llms.txt and post text; the venture's page and HTML are unchanged.
deviations.did: ran the venture's full test suite (349 tests) and the post checks

notes: Flagship open-tennis-robots (allocator row 7). Added an ESC_TAU frame (board reports ESC_TAU_US), kept the survey in the shot log, added a pre-drill check (stop calibration drills on a mismatch over 15%, exit 4), added the esc-lag command, and made the drill-end advice use the board's real setting. Local: run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots ok (349 tests, 194.5 s); check_post_frontmatter, check_post_links and post_similarity clean; portfolio validate.py clean. Sweep: tests/esc_lag_check_sweep.py, eval/esc-lag-check-sweep-2026-11-16.txt.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an embedded engineer adding a config-report frame, a log format change, a pre-run interlock, tests and a 72-case simulated sweep

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
